title: Reserved pool allocation stall under high-tenant-cardinality causing sustained shortfall
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a high-traffic window we observed a sustained shortfall in reserved capacity for several customers using Dedicated pools. The allocator appeared healthy but headroom accounting stopped increasing for affected pools, causing the autoscaler to avoid scaling up and customers to see elevated throttles and tail latency. This ticket covers investigation, emergency mitigation, hotfix rollout, and follow-up actions.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a testbench that creates ~3k tenants with small, varying reservation weights against a single reserved pool controller. 2) Submit bursty allocation and release patterns over 10 minutes (p50 interarrival 30ms). 3) Observe allocator leader CPU spike and reconciliation loop latency >2s, followed by headroom metric flatlining and subsequent failed allocation attempts. 4) Confirm that simulated customer traffic yields 10-30% request failures and increased enqueue latency.
impact_summary: Customer-facing: One large customer (Fabrikate) experienced sustained 25-35% request throttling over a 2 hour window starting 2025-02-18T21:12Z. Platform: two dedicated clusters had 18% effective capacity loss for minutes at a time. Operational: increased paging and support tickets; temporary manual capacity injections were needed for highest-tier tenants.
timeline: 2025-02-18 21:10Z - Alerts: reserved_pool_headroom flatline and scaler_suppress_count rising. 2025-02-18 21:25Z - Pager triggered; initial triage identified allocator reconciliation latency. 2025-02-18 21:40Z - Hotfix PR opened to rate-limit tenant delta processing and add defensive backpressure. 2025-02-18 22:08Z - Hotfix rolled to canary cluster; headroom recovered. 2025-02-19 00:20Z - Rollout completed across all affected clusters. 2025-03-03 - Postmortem and follow-ups finalized.
root_cause: The allocator reconciliation loop iterated over a high-cardinality set of tenant weight changes without batching or backpressure, causing the leader to spend excessive CPU and delay headroom recalculation. A non-linear worst-case in reconciliation work scheduling (O(n^2) in pathological delta patterns) meant that during churn the apparent available headroom did not surface to the autoscaler fast enough, preventing scale-ups and enabling throttling to persist.
mitigations_and_hotfix: Emergency hotfix (PR #4892) introduced: 1) bounded reconciliation queue with rate-limited worker concurrency; 2) opportunistic incremental headroom updates decoupled from full reconciliation; 3) short-term preemption policy to reclaim cold slots when headroom metrics stall. We deployed the hotfix to canary, validated headroom and allocation success rates, then promoted to all clusters. Metrics returned to normal within ~20 minutes post-rollout.
long_term_action_items: Implement batched tenant-delta aggregation upstream of allocator to reduce reconciliation pressure
Refactor reconciliation scheduler to guarantee O(n) worst-case behavior and add amortized cost tracking
Add synthetic high-cardinality churn tests to CI that exercise worst-case reconciliation paths
Enhance headroom telemetry with per-reconcile latency histograms and a stall detector alert
Document and expose a tenant-side guidance doc to reduce churn (rate limits for reservation updates)
customer_communications: Customer-facing status updates were posted to the support ticket (SUP-7831) and a follow-up call held with Fabrikate engineering on 2025-02-20. We explained the root cause, the hotfix, and committed to the long-term roadmap above. Fabrikate accepted the mitigation and requested a post-deployment verification run; we scheduled a joint test on 2025-03-05.
